chunk_findings.detail: The intent for this change specifies two tools: `ddflow_list` covering kinds `task|phase|bug|research|session`, **plus** `session show` exposed as its own tool `ddflow_show`. The README describes something different in three ways: (1) it folds `session show` into `ddflow_list` as `kind=session` with an `id` argument and never mentions `ddflow_show` at all; (2) it expands the `kind` set to `task|phase|bug|research|session|search`, adding `search`, which the intent's kind list omits; and (3) the table rows likewise advertise only `ddflow_list kind=search` / `ddflow_list (kind, state, phase, tag, owner, since, limit, all)`. Concretely, anyone (or any parity/budget test) following this documentation will call `ddflow_list` with `kind=session` and otherwise never learn that `ddflow_show` is supposed to exist, while the stated intent says the reverse. One of the two — the README or the implementation the intent describes — is wrong about the tool name/count, and since the change ships both the documentation and the implementation, the documented interface and the intended interface cannot both hold.

chunk_findings.detail: `_filters` is documented as "Echoed under the flag's own name: replaying `agent` would be identity," and it does `{("owner" if k == "agent" else k): v ...}`. It is applied to the session result (`data["filters"] = _filters(view.filters)`) and to the search result (`"filters": _filters(res.filters)`), but the generic list path does `out = view_list(repo, kind, state=..., phase=..., tag=..., agent=owner, ...)` and then `return out` with no normalization. `view_list` is the CLI-shared function whose parameter is `agent` (it is called with `agent=owner`), so its echoed filter dict keeps the internal key `agent`. The result is that the *same* tool emits two different filter-key shapes depending on `kind`: `ddflow_list(kind="task", owner="bob")` returns `filters: {"agent": "bob"}`, while `ddflow_list(kind="session", owner="bob")` returns `filters: {"owner": "bob"}`. A caller that replays the returned `filters` back into the tool, or a parity test comparing the MCP output against the session/search shape, sees `agent` for four kinds and `owner` for the other two. Either the list path needs `out.data["filters"] = _filters(out.data["filters"])` as well, or session/search must not rename.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/viewers.py:view_read (`_filters` application)

chunk_findings.detail: The `if id: return O.refused(...)` guard is placed *after* the `if kind == "search"` branch, so `ddflow_list(kind="search", id="s1")` silently returns search results with `id` ignored, whereas the same irrelevant `id` on `kind="task"/"phase"/"bug"/"research"` is explicitly refused with "id applies to kind=session". The author's own refusal message establishes that `id` is session-only, so `kind="search"` is the single kind where an inapplicable `id` is accepted without error, giving callers a silent wrong-input path instead of the refusal every other non-session kind gets.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/viewers.py:view_read (dispatch order of the `id` check)

chunk_findings.detail: The tool advertises `0 = all` in both the tool description ("25 rows unless `limit` (0 = all)") and the `limit` property ("Rows (default 25; 0 = all)"), but the implementation cannot honor that. The api maps `a.get("limit") == 0` to the literal `1000`, and it never clamps any other value: `int(a.get("limit") or 25)` passes e.g. `999999` straight to `view_read`. Consequently, on a repo with 1500 tasks, `ddflow_list kind=task limit=0` returns at most 1000 rows (`shown=1000`, `total=1500`) and the bound then emits the note "raise limit (0 = all, at most 1000)" — a remedy that is impossible because 0 already means 1000 and larger explicit values are not clamped to the documented "at most 1000" ceiling either. Either the cap must be enforced/clamped and the description corrected, or 0 must actually mean "all".

```

`LEAF_VIA` maps `("session", "show")` to `("ddflow_list", "session")`, i.e. it declares the `session show` leaf covered by the *list* viewer. That is not the tool the intent assigns to that leaf ("session show via `ddflow_show`"), and `ddflow_list --kind session` is a bounded row listing, not a single-session render — the `kind` values select a viewer, they do not select "show a record by id". Concretely, `leaf_covered(("session", "show"))` now returns `True` purely because the path is in `LEAF_VIA`, so the parity suite stays green even if the `ddflow_show` tool is never registered or is later deleted: the acceptance criterion "parity test green" is satisfied vacuously for `session show`, and the new `test_every_viewer_leaf_names_a_kind_ddflow_list_accepts` does not catch it because it only checks `tool in TOOLS` and `kind in READ_KINDS`, never that the mapped tool actually implements the leaf. The same mapping also feeds `_tool_for(("session", "show")) -> "ddflow_list"`, so the flag-divergence check now compares `session show`'s CLI flags against `ddflow_list`'s parameter set, which can either mask a real divergence (any `--kind`-shaped flag hits the `("ddflow_list", "--kind")` exemption whose stated reason, "carried by `sources`", is about `ddflow search`, not about `session show`) or spuriously fail on a `show`-specific flag that was never exempted. Either way the entry asserts coverage that the table's own docstring ("the `kind` that selects it") does not support for a show leaf.

chunk_findings.detail: The tool description and the `limit` property both promise "0 = all", and `bound_list`'s note promises "at most 1000", but the code implements neither: `limit=0` is rewritten to 1000, so in any repo with more than 1000 matching rows a caller who asks for "all" silently gets only the newest 1000 with `truncated=True`, and the note then tells them to "raise limit (0 = all, at most 1000)", which is a no-op (0 is already the documented maximum). At the same time explicit values are never clamped: a call like `ddflow_list{kind:"task", limit:100000}` forwards `100000` to `view_read`, and the list branch of `bound_list` returns the body untouched (it only appends a note), so the payload the change is supposed to bound can be made arbitrarily large — defeating the "bounded payloads via mcp_bound" acceptance. If 1000 is the intended ceiling, the lambda should be `min(int(a.get("limit") or 25), 1000)` with 0 mapped to the ceiling, and the description/note should say "0 = all (up to 1000)".

chunk_findings.detail: When session entries are clipped, the note reads "`ddflow session show <id>` has them whole." That names a CLI command (`ddflow session show`), not an MCP tool. The MCP surface has no tool with a space-containing name (all entries in `BOUNDS`/the tool table are `ddflow_*`, and the intent states session show is reached via `ddflow_show`); the sibling description text even points at the MCP tool `ddflow_history` by tool name. An agent that follows the note will issue a call to a nonexistent tool and get an "unknown tool" error instead of the full entry text.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py — `bound_list` session note

chunk_findings.detail:
The change declares `("session", "show"): ("ddflow_list", "session")`, but the intent for this work is `session show` served by a separate `ddflow_show` tool ("plus session show via ddflow_show"), not by `ddflow_list` with `kind=session` (which is the session *list* viewer and cannot return a single session's detail).

Because `leaf_covered()` now short-circuits on `path in LEAF_VIA`, the ratchet will report `session show` as covered even if `ddflow_show` does not exist, is broken, or loses a flag — e.g. deleting the `ddflow_show` tool/registration and re-running `tests/test_mcp_parity.py` still passes, and the new `test_every_viewer_leaf_names_a_kind_ddflow_list_accepts` also passes because it only checks `"ddflow_list" in TOOLS`. Likewise `_tool_for(("session", "show"))` returns `ddflow_list`, so any per-leaf flag/parameter parity assertion for `session show` is evaluated against `ddflow_list`'s schema instead of `ddflow_show`'s, masking a real divergence between the CLI leaf and the tool that actually serves it. The correct mapping for this leaf is the tool named in the intent (or an explicit exemption until it lands), not `ddflow_list`/`session`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_parity.py — `LEAF_VIA[("session", "show")]`

chunk_findings.detail: The hunk lowers `TOOLS_LIST_BUDGET` from 93,500 to 91,500 on the strength of two claims that this diff does not substantiate: (a) `ddflow_list` costs ~1.3 KB and (b) shrinking the shared `as_agent` description from 113 to 66 characters saves "-4 KB". Claim (b) implies the 47-character reduction is repeated on the order of ~85 tools to reach 4 KB; if the server actually exposes far fewer tools, the real saving shrinks proportionally. The pre-change comment records that the tree already sat at 91,958 bytes against the old 93,500 limit, i.e. only 1,542 bytes of headroom. Reaching 91,500 therefore requires the measured byte count to fall by at least 458 bytes net, which is not demonstrated anywhere in this hunk. If the `as_agent` trim is repeated on fewer tools than assumed, the new tool's ~1.3 KB is not fully offset and the budget assertion fails on the exact inputs it is meant to guard. This is flagged only because the arithmetic in the comment cannot be reconciled from the diff alone; if the sibling hunks contain the measured byte count proving the reduction, the finding is void.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py:17 — unverifiable budget reduction

chunk_findings.detail:
The change routes session *show* through `ddflow_list(kind="session", id="S1")` and asserts that `ddflow_list` returns a full session body (`{"id": ..., "entries": [...]}`), and `test_one_tool_not_six` only verifies `ddflow_list`'s description size. The stated intent is explicitly "one `ddflow_list` tool (kind=task|phase|bug|research|session) **plus session show via `ddflow_show`**". Two concrete problems follow from this mismatch:

1. If the implementation actually honors the intent and exposes session-show as the separate `ddflow_show` tool (so `ddflow_list` only accepts `kind`/filters and not `id`), then the client in this change's own test (`_call(proj, kind="session", id="S1")`, line 109) is calling the wrong tool: `ddflow_list` will ignore `id` (or refuse it, as `test_refusals` expects for `{"kind":"task","id":"S1"}` at line 118), so `body` has no `entries` key and line 109 raises `KeyError` — the acceptance test for "session show" fails.
2. Conversely, if the change folded session-show into `ddflow_list` (as the diff docstring implies), then the required `ddflow_show` tool is never created or verified: `test_one_tool_not_six` only budget-checks `TOOLS["ddflow_list"]["description"]`, and no test references `ddflow_show`, so an MCP client invoking `ddflow_show` per the documented API gets an "unknown tool" error and the tool's contribution to the 93,500-byte tools/list budget is never asserted.

Either reading is inconsistent with the stated API, and the test file provides no assertion that distinguishes them (nor that `ddflow_show` exists).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_view_mcp.py:109 (test_session_id_shows_one_session_in_full) and tests/test_view_mcp.py:124 (test_one_tool_not_six)
```

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_TAKES` table omits `tag` for `bug`, while `task`, `phase` and `research` all accept it and `view_list` is called with `tag=tag` uniformly for every list kind. The change's own README (line ~3243) lists `tag` among the CLI selectors (`state`, `phase`, `tag`, `owner`, `since`, `all`), and the MCP schema gives `tag` no kind qualifier ("Only this tag.") while `all` is explicitly scoped ("kind=bug: ..."), so `tag` is presented as a general selector. Input: `ddflow_list(kind="bug", tag="regression")` now hits the stray check and returns `kind=bug has no tag (it takes: all, phase)` instead of the filtered bug rows the CLI and the previous code path produced by forwarding `tag` into the engine. This is both a behavior regression and an MCP/CLI parity break; add `"tag"` to `_TAKES["bug"]` (or, if the bug engine truly rejects tags, the README/schema must say so).

chunk_findings.detail: The description and the `limit` parameter were changed to claim `0 = the most: 1000`, but the README changed in the same diff states `0 = the most: 1000 for a list, 200 for a search`, and for `kind=session` `limit=0` means all entries ("`limit=0` for all"), not 1000. So for `kind=search` the tool description overstates the cap by 5x. A model that reads the description and calls `kind=search, limit=0` expecting up to 1000 rows gets 200 plus a cut notice; the description (the only text the model sees) should mention the per-kind bounds or drop the concrete number.

The change routes session *show* through `ddflow_list(kind="session", id="S1")` and asserts that `ddflow_list` returns a full session body (`{"id": ..., "entries": [...]}`), and `test_one_tool_not_six` only verifies `ddflow_list`'s description size. The stated intent is explicitly "one `ddflow_list` tool (kind=task|phase|bug|research|session) **plus session show via `ddflow_show`**". Two concrete problems follow from this mismatch:

1. If the implementation actually honors the intent and exposes session-show as the separate `ddflow_show` tool (so `ddflow_list` only accepts `kind`/filters and not `id`), then the client in this change's own test (`_call(proj, kind="session", id="S1")`, line 109) is calling the wrong tool: `ddflow_list` will ignore `id` (or refuse it, as `test_refusals` expects for `{"kind":"task","id":"S1"}` at line 118), so `body` has no `entries` key and line 109 raises `KeyError` — the acceptance test for "session show" fails.
2. Conversely, if the change folded session-show into `ddflow_list` (as the diff docstring implies), then the required `ddflow_show` tool is never created or verified: `test_one_tool_not_six` only budget-checks `TOOLS["ddflow_list"]["description"]`, and no test references `ddflow_show`, so an MCP client invoking `ddflow_show` per the documented API gets an "unknown tool" error and the tool's contribution to the 93,500-byte tools/list budget is never asserted.

Either reading is inconsistent with the stated API, and the test file provides no assertion that distinguishes them (nor that `ddflow_show` exists).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_view_mcp.py:109 (test_session_id_shows_one_session_in_full) and tests/test_view_mcp.py:124 (test_one_tool_not_six)

chunk_findings.detail: The `bug` entry omits `tag`, even though the tool's own documented selector set lists `tag` as a general filter (`README.md:3243`: the CLI's `state`, `phase`, `tag`, `owner`, `since`, `all` for bugs) and every other list kind admits it (`task`: `{phase, tag}`, `phase`: `{tag}`, `research`: `{phase, tag}`). With the new stray-check, a call like `ddflow_list kind=bug tag=<x>` now builds `stray = ["tag"]` and returns `view.read` refused with `"kind=bug has no tag ..."` instead of the tagged bug rows. So a filter the reader was previously allowed to pass (and that the docs say is valid) now errors out; either `tag` must be added to the `bug` set, or the generic selector documentation is wrong and needs narrowing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/viewers.py:64 (the `"bug": frozenset({"phase", "all"})` entry)

chunk_findings.detail: The description text `"0 = the most: 1000"` and the parameter doc `"Rows (default 25; 0 = the most, 1000)."` both advertise 1000 as the `limit=0` cap for any kind, but the README changed in this same diff says a search is capped differently (`"0 = the most: 1000 for a list, 200 for a search"`). The MCP description is what a client/model actually sees, so `ddflow_list kind=search limit=0` promises up to 1000 rows while the search path only yields at most 200; the tool description is inaccurate for `kind=search`. The `1000` wording should be qualified (or the search cap stated) to match the documented behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:1312 and mcp.py:1325

chunk_findings.detail: The test is named/claimed as covering the owner-filter echo "for every kind", and the change's stated acceptance is that *each* kind (`task|phase|bug|research|session`) behaves, but the loop body is `for kind in ("task", "session")`, so `phase`, `bug`, and `research` are never exercised. Demonstration: if the part-1 implementation echoes the owner filter under a different key (or drops it) specifically on the `phase`, `bug`, or `research` branches of the consolidated `ddflow_list`, this test still passes green, while a client calling `_call(proj, kind="bug", owner="alice", limit=5)` would receive a `filters` payload that does not contain `"owner": "alice"` — exactly the regression the test's name asserts it guards, and exactly what the "MCP parity ratchet / each kind" acceptance requires. Only the two kinds that were probably also covered by the pre-existing task/session paths are checked.
